guide.summary: A fort, museums, a theatre and an island aquarium, with breakfast cafés, Caribbean dinners and cocktail bars in the walled city and Getsemaní, checked against their own websites.
highlights: Castillo de San Felipe de Barajas
Santuario y Museo San Pedro Claver
Museo de Arte Moderno de Cartagena
guide.tip: The Museo de Arte Moderno is closed on Mondays and Restaurante Don Juan is closed on Sundays, while the Museo Histórico and the San Pedro Claver museum list opening hours every day of the week.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.value: Museo de Arte Moderno: Mondays; Restaurante Don Juan: Sundays
toolkit.copy: The Museo de Arte Moderno lists "Lunes: Cerrado", and Restaurante Don Juan says the house rests on Sundays. The Museo Histórico de Cartagena and the Santuario y Museo San Pedro Claver both list hours for Sundays and holidays.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.value: Castillo tickets online; museum tariffs published
toolkit.copy: The fort operator sells Castillo de San Felipe de Barajas tickets online and lists a full rate of COP 25,000, with free entry for Colombians on the last Sunday of each month except January and December. The Museo Histórico lists adults at COP 24,000 and free entry for under-fives.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Alquímico says it takes no reservations and recommends arriving before 8 p.m. to get in. Celele, La Vitrola, Juan del Mar and Restaurante Don Juan all link to online booking from their own sites.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.value: Dress code, no minors, no pets at the fort
toolkit.copy: Alquímico admits no minors and asks for casual-formal dress, with no beachwear or sportswear. At the Castillo, animals other than guide dogs are not allowed, and the operator advises comfortable shoes because of steep ramps and slippery tunnels.

guide.dek: Book the Castillo and your dinners online, keep Mondays for sights other than the Museo de Arte Moderno, and arrive early for walk-in bars.
intro: Every place in this guide was checked against its own website or the public body that runs it. Start with the Castillo de San Felipe de Barajas on Avenida Antonio Arévalo, where the operator, Escuela Taller Cartagena de Indias, sells entry online with the promise of no queues. Its English page lists a full rate of COP 25,000 and free entry for Colombians on the last Sunday of each month, except January and December. Bring comfortable shoes and water: the operator warns of steep ramps, slippery tunnels and midday heat, and only guide dogs are allowed inside.

Inside the walls, the Santuario y Museo San Pedro Claver at Carrera 4 #30-01 lists hours every day, from 9 a.m. on weekdays and 10 a.m. at weekends and on holidays. The Museo Histórico de Cartagena, in the Palacio de la Inquisición on Plaza de Bolívar, lists adult tickets at COP 24,000, with under-fives free. Plan around Mondays for the Museo de Arte Moderno on Plaza San Pedro Claver, which says it is closed that day. For an evening out, the city's heritage institute runs the Teatro Adolfo Mejía on Plaza de la Merced and has announced its 2026 season.

For dinner, Celele on Calle del Espíritu Santo in Getsemaní describes contemporary Caribbean cooking built on the region's produce, and Alma sits inside Casa San Agustín, which calls itself a 2026 two Michelin Keys winner. Restaurante Don Juan on Avenida Carlos Escallón lists weekday lunches and dinners from Monday to Saturday and is closed on Sundays. La Vitrola lists live Cuban son every night from 8 p.m., while La Cevichería in San Diego lists service from noon to 11 p.m. daily. Juan del Mar, a restaurant and pizzeria on Plaza de San Diego, takes bookings online.

For drinks, Alquímico on Calle del Colegio opens nightly from 7 p.m. but takes no reservations, admits no minors and asks for casual-formal dress, so you should aim to arrive before 8 p.m. El Barón on Plaza San Pedro Claver opens from 4 p.m. Monday to Thursday and from noon at weekends. For a quieter coffee, Ábaco Libros y Café pairs books and coffee from 8 a.m. Monday to Saturday. Further out, the Oceanario Islas del Rosario on Isla San Martín de Pajarales lists daily hours of 9 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., so it suits a morning boat trip.
summaryCards: Book the Castillo de San Felipe de Barajas online, then walk into the walled city for the Museo Histórico de Cartagena and the Santuario y Museo San Pedro Claver.
Have breakfast at Di Silvio Trattoria's Getsemaní branch, browse Ábaco Libros y Café, and reach the Museo de Arte Moderno once it opens at 11 a.m. on any day except Monday, when it is closed.
Reserve Celele, La Vitrola or Restaurante Don Juan online, remembering that Don Juan is closed on Sundays, but plan to queue early for Alquímico, which takes walk-ins only.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability, and most sites read carry no dated 2026 hours notice, so hours are reported as each site lists them. The Castillo's hours come from an undated operator page that conflicts with an older 2023 notice (7 a.m. versus 8 a.m. opening), and Di Silvio's Getsemaní opening time differs between its branch page and FAQ. Celele, Alma, Erre, Townhouse and the Teatro Adolfo Mejía publish no opening hours. Sites that could not be read include the Museo del Oro Zenú (bot check), Restaurante Interno (expired certificate), Café Havana (DNS failure), Época and Libertario (rate-limited), Carmen and María (domains now redirect elsewhere) and the national park page for Corales del Rosario (404). No bakery could be confirmed: Pastelería Mila's only listed address is marked "coming soon", so the bakery list is empty.
